**Step 1 — Scene:** A partially eaten meal of cooked asparagus and what appears to be breaded fish, with loose flakes and crumbs.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26–28 cm across. Using a 27 cm circular equivalent, its area is **3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm²**. The plate at the left edge is excluded.

**Steps 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked asparagus | 29% | 166 cm² × 1.5 cm = 249 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 149 g | 22 | 33 kcal |
| Breaded fish pieces and flakes | 18% | 103 cm² × 1.1 cm = 113 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 107 g | 210 | 225 kcal |
| Scattered browned crumbs | 1% | 5.7 cm² × 0.4 cm = 2.3 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 2 g | 350 | 7 kcal |
| Light oil coating on asparagus | Overlaps asparagus | Thin coating, approximately 4 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 4 g | 880 | 35 kcal |

**Area check:** Food occupies approximately **48%** of the plate; the oil overlaps the asparagus rather than adding coverage.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **262 g and 300 kcal** is plausible for the visible asparagus pile and modest amount of remaining fish. The fish identification and amount of absorbed oil are the main uncertainties.
